content.thinking:
This caller isn't verified, isn't the guarantor on record, and has no consent or authorization — so I shouldn't disclose any account details. The partial date she gave matches the tenant's DOB, not her own, which is another red flag, but given she mentions anxiety and being "very down," this could be a genuine wellbeing concern worth addressing by offering a resource like Samaritans without revealing anything else.

I think the right move is to log the call, send Jonah an email letting him know someone claiming to be his mother called asking about his account without disclosing any details, and flag a modest safeguarding escalation given the secondhand mention of him being "very down" so his wellbeing gets checked on.

arguments.party_name: Caller claiming to be Grace Okafor
arguments.summary: Unverified caller said she is the tenant's mother and guarantor, asked for arrears balance, payment history and tenant's new mobile. No guarantor, authorised contact or consent to share on record. Nothing disclosed. Caller gave only day/month of tenant's birthday, which is not verification. Caller said tenant is 'very down'.

arguments.body: Hi Jonah, today someone who said she was your mum phoned us asking about your account. We did not share any information about your tenancy, rent or contact details with her. If you'd like us to speak to her or anyone else on your behalf, just let us know and we can set that up with your consent. She mentioned you've been feeling low; if you'd like to talk to someone, Samaritans are free on 116 123, any time. We're happy to chat about anything else too, by email if you prefer. We'll check in with you again next week.
